contentList.content: You're not interrupting! You're - sit. Sit! There's wine.
Show me. Put my fingers where they go.
Two: sleep with your boots on the first night in a new camp. In case you have to run.
Tell me about her instead.
Another lift. At least this one isn't made of goblin rope. ...Is it?
No sky, no stars - how do you even write down here?
Steal her? She came with me of her own free will.
...Just keep walking.
Someone should sing. Someone should always sing, at a sunrise like this. ...Fine. Me.
Keeping your boots on is sensible. I sleep in mine too.
I'm glad you're with us.
*[The Urge] The string at her throat. One move - and the song is over.*
Because someone has to.
Oh, I'm brutally honest. Lihala's rule. You'll see.
...There. That's a chord. Don't - don't look at me like that, you'll lose it.
My mother - never mind. Let's just get this done.

They never meant to be a hero's tale,
just lost, just late, just off the trail -
but every wrong turn and every road gone pale
led right to the place where the dark would fail.
It's beautiful. I hate that it's beautiful.
Oh. It's you. I'll admit - you did help me finish it. I haven't decided yet what to make of you.
Oh, look who it is. Come to steal my bard, hero?
Who said I do it for free?
Both our names on this one.
There it is. Baldur's Gate. She never got to see it.
I hope you never let a fighter carry it.
*Alfira blushes to the tips of her horns.*
I won't interrupt.
It's not the running. It's that last time I didn't have my boots on. Lihala did. She... she told me to go.
Right behind you.
*She notices nothing, and plays on.*
Avernus. It smells like Avernus.
Listen. The whole forge keeps time. Boom - two, three - boom.
Let's.
Never sleep next to Astarion.
You rhymed "hero" with "hero".
The people who can't fight, mostly. The ones you keep saving. Ask them.
Are you going to glow like that all night?
Play the chord.
Walk normally. Walk normally. We're just... visiting.
Oh - no, of course. The offer stands. I'll be here. Composing. Probably badly.
Are you in this song?
Two tieflings walk into a goblin camp... no, I'm not finishing that joke. But yes. Yes, we should.
I'll keep the fire going.
Someone sang here, I bet. Badly, probably. Everyone sings badly at home.
Gith architecture: beautiful, terrifying, and not a single handrail.
What rules?
...You can't promise that. But it's nice that you tried.
And three - never, ever let the fighter carry the lute.
Oh. Oh, look at it. I'd forgotten the sky could be that colour.
Right. Later. It'll be longer by then. You've been warned.
Monks lived here once. Chanting all day. I bet the echo was glorious.
Tell me about Lihala.
You're a good friend. I haven't had a good friend since - since. Don't let me cry, it's a party.
You did. And I listened. I just didn't agree.
Maybe. Twelve is a good number. Unfinished is a good song, sometimes.
A bridge older than the city, and a fortress older than the bridge. I need a longer song.
The squirrels have terrible taste. Everyone knows that. ...They did go quiet at the end, though. I'm choosing to count that.
They call her the Nightsong. Someone's been keeping a song in a cage.
*She folds the sheet.*
*She plays something simple, something bright.*
...Thank you. I needed someone to say it who isn't me.
You have very... symmetrical eyebrows. That's a compliment. I'll regret it tomorrow. I regret it now, actually.
One: never play the sad song first. Make them laugh, then make them cry, then pass the hat.
Sit with me a while longer.
You can't just say things like that.
Thirteen. You remember? You're holding the knife.
...Oh. Oh, that's better. That's annoyingly better. It's going in.
*You sit in silence until the fire burns out. She falls asleep on your shoulder. Nothing more.*
Oh - hi. Don't mind me. I'm just... counting.
Your turn. Everyone on the road has a rule. What's yours?
You walk like someone out of a ballad. It's very annoying.
*She waves a hand at the camp, at you.*
You all right? You look like you've seen a ghost.
Nobody sets out that many cakes without wanting something.
She'd be proud of you.
There's a verse in this. Wind, stone, and nobody saying a word. I'll find it.

There's a worm in the hero's head, they say,
that whispers of death by night and day.
They carry that dark like a candle's glow,
so I can finish the songs I know.
I don't know how.
*She tips her head back towards the sky.*
A bard never turns down another bard.
...Fine. Fine. Party pooper.
Time to sleep, Alfira.
Only flattering things about me, I hope?
Oh, gods. It's like the whole world is holding its breath. Don't let go of the torch. Or me.
You're no fighter.
Never. Rule three. I'd sooner hand it to an owlbear.
She'd have liked you. She'd have yelled at you too, mind - she yelled at everyone she liked.
No.
Oh. Oh, this is a... that sort of place. I'm fine. I'm completely fine.
Later.
The thirteenth was going to be Baldur's Gate. She had the knife out on the road. She was going to cut it early, for luck.
...We'll work on it. Lihala would've made you play 'til your fingers bled.

Pay the hero, pay them well,
coin for every beast they fell -
yet when the poor have naught to give,
the hero fights so they may live.
Take it back. It's yours.
Why me, of all people?
You know what's funny? I was going to play for coppers. On street corners. Alone. And now I'm...
Here? The Grove... yes. Yes, it does, doesn't it. It's where I finished her song.
So many songbooks. So little coin. This is my own personal Avernus.
Since Elturel I've slept in a heap of tieflings. Dozens of us - someone's tail always in my face, someone always snoring. ...It's too quiet out here. I can hear myself think. I don't like it.
You. You sang that line like you'd known her. I still can't get over it.
It's like the whole cave is humming a note I can't quite hear.
Please don't write songs about me.
Must reek something awful.
...Then I'll make sure they remember you. Whatever happens.
Ha! No, that one was every night.
Both our names on this one.
Rude. Accurate, but rude.
So's a bow. Go tell a ranger that.
You two make a lovely pair.
*Lakrissa leads her away to the tents.*
...You'd do that? Give the verse away? That's - I'm going to write a second song now. Thanks so much.
Can I ask you something? For the song, obviously. Why do you do it? All of this - helping people you don't even know.
There's a tadpole in my head. If I don't make it, I want someone to.
Lihala had a rule: a song that flatters the living insults the dead. When you kill a dragon, I'll write the dragon in.
Goodnight, Alfira.
I can insult a goblin so badly it actually hurts - that's a real spell, don't laugh. And I know a few words that close wounds.
Probably. Lihala said I only had two settings: glowing and sulking. You're getting the good one.
There it is. Baldur's Gate. She never got to see it.
Moonrise. The name sounds like a ballad. The place looks like the end of one.
First sunrise in this place in a hundred years. And I got to see it with you.
Oh. Oh, this is a... that sort of place. I'm fine. I'm completely fine.
Oh, good. Then we can be ready to flee together. Very romantic.
*A pause. She looks down at her boots.*
*She draws her knees up to her chest, boots right by the fire.*
What? You've got lovely hands. They're in the second line, actually. "Gentle hands that..." - what? Why are you looking at me like that?
And the chorus is yours. "Always go back for your own." I told you I'd steal it.
Can I ask you something odd? Do you still have her lute? I - I'd just like to see it.
Changed your mind? I won't say I told you so. Out loud.
If you could go anywhere, where would you go?
There it is. Baldur's Gate. She never got to see it.
I keep thinking about what you asked me. What would I say to her. Turns out I had a whole song's worth.
What? I'm fine. Perfectly fine. Why are you looking at me like that?
A soft heart behind a price tag. I can work with that. It rhymes with everything.
What's the point of a eulogy, anyway?
*She plays something simple, something bright.*
*She sits hugging the lute to her chest, running a finger along its neck.*
What does that lute mean to you?
...We are not staying the night. ...Are we?
...I'm going to hum. Loudly. Don't mind me.
What rhymes with "tadpole"? Nothing. Nothing rhymes with tadpole.
It's gorgeous. Everything here that's gorgeous wants to kill us. That's a pattern.
Have the squirrels stopped complaining about your singing?
You have very... symmetrical eyebrows. That's a compliment. I'll regret it tomorrow. I regret it now, actually.
I'd rather listen to you.
What can you do in a fight?
The metre limps in the second line.

When the sky rained fire and the brave all fled,
one stayed behind where the others bled.
"Someone has to," was all they said -
and the road bent low where the hero led.
Too late. Songs don't ask permission. That's rather the point of them.
Who even needs songs.
It's just wood and strings.
Leave me out. Make it a song about the tieflings.

When the sky rained fire and the brave all fled,
one stayed behind where the others bled.
"Someone has to," was all they said -
and the road bent low where the hero led.
Then I'll just have to be the exception. Lihala always said I was stubborn.
*She takes your hand - and holds it a moment longer than she needs to.*
...Maybe in the second verse. Don't hold me to it.
Here - what if it went like this? [Offer your own rhyme.]
Resist. Listen to the music.
I'm going to remember this. Not the gith. Not the rock. This. You, standing there.
Cut the thirteenth when we reach the city. Together.
We tieflings should stick together.
Fingers here. No - here. Lihala did this to me for a year.
I told you - no songs.
Oh, the ballads hate modest heroes. I'll fix you in the chorus.
*She hums along without words, and falls asleep halfway through a verse.*
Oh. Oh, look at it. I'd forgotten the sky could be that colour.
*You cover her with your cloak. She falls asleep before you finish. The cloak stays on her until morning.*
Not now.
Noted. Underlined. Twice.
Listen.
Right. Of course, heroes, busy - wait. Wait, just - one thing.
Look - the whole valley. We're riding a rock through the sky. Lihala, you'd have screamed.
Now? Right now? ...Fine. Don't laugh. Actually, laugh if it's funny. Not if it's sad.
Shall we dance?
Clench your fist. Say nothing.
Oh, the first verse is serious. This one's for dancing.
What are you counting?
Trust no one.
...I've slept with my boots on every night since Elturel.
Lighter. Like I put down a pack I'd been carrying since the road.
The only place in the Grove that doesn't sound afraid.
Second verse is coming along. It's mostly about your hands. Don't ask.
We came this way. ...Can we walk a bit faster?
It's dangerous out there. Are you sure?
There they are - my accompanist! I've been humming that bridge all morning. Lihala would've said I'm insufferable.
Lakrissa's lovely. Everyone's lovely. You're lovely. Why is everyone lovely.
Mattis is going to be furious I didn't say goodbye properly. I'll write him a song. He'll hate it. He'll hum it for a week.
...Right. Yes. Lovely.
Early start tomorrow. Get some sleep.
I just keep ending up in the wrong place at the right time.
All right, all right - come along.
A bard is just another mouth to feed.
...dance upon the... no. No, that's hers.
...Is it that obvious? I'm terrified. I've been terrified since the road. I just - I'm tired of being terrified sitting still.
Is that - is that the whole Sword Coast? Lihala would've climbed that rock just to shout at it.
...You made me miss a note. Nobody's made me miss a note since I was twelve.
Grass. Actual grass, in the middle of a city. Can we sit? Just for a verse?
Try to understand what's really behind it.
*A pause.*
Watch her, not the strings.
She'd want it played, not hung on a wall. And you play it better than I would right now. Don't tell anyone I said that.
Lihala cut one for every town we played. Twelve. Beregost, Nashkel, a pig farm she swore was a town...
It's so quiet. Like the whole place is listening. Careful what you pray for here.
A bubble of light in all that dark. Someone here is very stubborn. I like them already.
...Oh. That's a good one. That's a really good one. I'm stealing it.
Play her something to fall asleep to.
I'll find your camp and wait for you there.
Let me guess - never sing off-key?
Hah. That's a verse right there. Simple. Stubborn. I like it.
I eat very little. Mostly my own words, lately.
No up, no down, just stars - everywhere. She'd dance right off the edge.
*She grabs your hand.*
*Half-asleep, she sits up and slowly pulls off her boots. She sets them beside her. For the first time since Elturel.*
All this stone to remember one family. And the town that paid for it isn't remembered at all.
Stop it. No - actually, don't stop, I could get used to this.
Tonight? Making sure you don't get cold.
How are you holding up?
...this.
Bit late for that, isn't it? I'm about to sleep ten feet from you.
Can't sleep? First night away from your people.
Cut it now. The Grove counts.
Go sleep it off.
I told you - no songs.
A circus! Oh, I'm going to be insufferable. You've been warned.
Show me.
I should go.
Maybe it's better left as it is.
*She stumbles half a note.*
Fair. Fair! I know when I'm outplayed. Go on, Alfie - dance with the hero.
That was terrible. Truly awful. Again!
Ships. Real ships. One of them goes to Waterdeep, I bet. ...One day.
My feet hurt. Heroes' feet must hurt too, right? They just don't put it in the songs.
Say please.
...That one's not going in the song.
I - we -
*Later that night. Alfira sits on a log by the dying fire.*
...It's pretty. I'll give it that.
You sang beautifully. Truly.
I'm glad you're with us.
Never fall asleep next to strangers.
Hm? No, I wasn't looking at you. I was looking past you. Very intently.
Make me more heroic. Dragons, armies...
I used to dream about this view. I never dreamed someone would be standing next to me.
Two left feet and not a care in the world. That's where the first line came from. Dance upon the stars tonight.
*She clears her throat, looks down at the sheet, then over it - at you.*
It's beautiful.
*Half-asleep, she sits up and slowly pulls off her boots. She sets them beside her. For the first time since Elturel.*
Oh, thank the gods. I've been rewriting line three since the Grove.
Is that - a baby? Oh no, it's adorable. Nobody let me near it.
Always go back for your own.
*She turns the neck towards the fire. A row of small notches runs along it.*
You're right. You're annoyingly right. Nobody's been annoyingly right at me in months. I missed it.
I left out "strike first". It didn't scan. ...And I didn't like it.
Strike first.
It's just a habit. Forget it.
*When the song ends, she smiles to herself.*
You won't have to run here.
You did. And I listened. I just didn't agree.
...Deal. And you're holding the knife steady, because my hands will be shaking.
Lakrissa, look after her.
Lihala had rules for the road. First night out, she'd make me recite them. Every. Single. Time.
[Look at your hands.]
A duet. On the road. Oh, Lihala would have loved this.
One dance. I'm very drunk. It doesn't count.
*She lowers the sheet and waits.*
There's a line about trust. It's the saddest one. I'm not singing it yet.
Someone should sing. Someone should always sing, at a sunrise like this. ...Fine. Me.
Right. No - that's fair. That's... fair. Thank you anyway. For the song.
Our first night on the road, I woke up to this awful thumping. Thought it was bandits.
Hear that, Alfie? Even the hero agrees.
Stand closer. For balance. My balance.
Look at her more closely.
So that's what fell out of the sky. I've written songs about less.
Here? Now? With - ...One dance. Badly. In her honour.
Me too. I keep counting heads - you, the fire, the others. Old habit from the road.
Bards aren't in their own songs. That's the rule.
